title: Cocktail 2 Is the Most Anticipated Indian Film on IMDb. It Has Already Recovered Half Its ₹150 Crore Budget.
excerpt: Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna's June 19 release tops IMDb's real-time rankings with a 21% page view share — nearly triple the next closest Bollywood film.
body:
Fourteen years after Saif Ali Khan, Deepika Padukone, and Diana Penty turned a Homi Adajania love triangle into a sleeper hit that became a defining film of NRI-era Bollywood, the franchise is back. And by every available measure, the audience is ready.

Cocktail 2, starring Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna, has reached the top of IMDb's real-time list of the most anticipated Indian movies and shows of 2026. The film currently holds a 21 per cent page view share on the platform — nearly triple the share commanded by Akshay Kumar's Welcome To The Jungle, which sits at number six with just over 7 per cent. The ranking is based on user engagement and page visits, making it a reflection of organic audience curiosity rather than paid promotion.

## A ₹150 Crore Bet That Is Already Paying Off

The production is one of the most expensive romantic comedies in Hindi cinema history. According to Bollywood Hungama, the total cost of Cocktail 2 stands at approximately ₹150 crore: ₹95 crore in production costs, ₹35 crore in combined fees for the three leads, and ₹20 crore allocated to print and publicity. In a market where romantic dramas are typically made at a fraction of that budget, the scale is a deliberate statement.

What makes the economics more interesting is that roughly 50 per cent of the budget has reportedly been recovered through pre-sales — satellite, digital, and music rights — before a single ticket has been sold. Dinesh Vijan's Maddock Films, which is co-producing with Luv Ranjan's Luv Films, has positioned the film not as a modest rom-com but as a major cinematic event. It was shot over 70 days across multiple international locations, including Sicily.

## The Diaspora Connection

For Indians abroad, the original Cocktail held a particular resonance. Its London setting, its frank treatment of modern relationships among young Indians navigating Western freedoms and family expectations, and its willingness to let Deepika Padukone play a character who drank, partied, and loved without apology — all of it felt closer to lived experience than the sanitised NRI families of most Bollywood films of that era.

The sequel carries different stars but the same creative team at the helm. Director Homi Adajania returns alongside Pritam Chakraborty on the music. The trailer, launched on May 29, has amplified the buzz with songs that have already begun circulating on playlists. Arijit Singh and Sunidhi Chauhan feature on the track Tujhko, while the Mashooka number, shot in Sicily, is being positioned as a chartbuster.

## What the Cast Brings

Shahid Kapoor reunites with Kriti Sanon after their 2024 hit Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya, which proved the pair's on-screen chemistry has commercial legs. Rashmika Mandanna, who has been steadily building a pan-India presence after Pushpa and Animal, joins what the makers describe as a contemporary love story about romance, heartbreak, friendship, and the mess in between.

The film releases in cinemas on June 19, entering a month that is already Bollywood's most crowded of 2026. It will have to hold its own against the aftermath of Peddi's opening wave, the anticipation for Diljit Dosanjh's Main Vaapas Aaunga a week earlier, and Welcome To The Jungle arriving the week after.

## What Is at Stake

The original Cocktail earned approximately ₹120 crore worldwide on a modest budget. Its cultural impact far outweighed its box office — it revived Diana Penty's modelling career, gave Deepika one of her most celebrated roles, and proved that Hindi cinema could tell stories about young urban Indians without moralising about their choices.

For the sequel, the financial stakes are higher and the audience expectations are more specific. The film needs to justify its ₹150 crore price tag, hold its own in a brutally competitive June calendar, and deliver a story that feels as fresh and unapologetic as the original did in 2012. The IMDb numbers and pre-sale recoveries suggest the audience is showing up. What remains to be seen is whether the film itself will match the appetite.

*Sources: Sacnilk, Bollywood Hungama, Zoom TV Entertainment, IMDb*
